To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of pumps, heat exchangers and fittings can be determined by using the same approach as for single-phase fluids.
the performance of pumps is reliable in the range of ice concentrations from 0 to 30 wt% and that pressure loss in fittings increases with increasing ice concentration.

ice slurry can be pumped by multiple-stage centrifugal pump with a performance that decreases with increasing ice concentrations, and that flow behaviour and pressure drop in single components of an ice slurry piping system are influenced by ice concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of components in an ice slurry system.
ice slurry systems in the temperature range from 0 °C to -5 °C.
the performance of components of ice slurries, i.e. pumps, heat exchangers and pipe fittings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ice slurries behave like conventional fluids with regard to the operation of pumps and flow in piping components, but that their performance is reduced by the increasing viscosity.
ice slurry can be pumped and handled in piping components with the same reliability as water.
the performance of pumps and piping system components is satisfactory and that ice slurry can be handled in piping systems without any problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ice slurry can be pumped reliably in a piping system with a multiple-stage centrifugal pump and that the flow behaviour in piping components is similar to the one of water.
ice slurry can be pumped with conventional pumps and that the flow behaviour of ice slurries in piping systems is similar to that of water.
ice slurry systems can be operated in a reliable and safe manner and that the performance of the system components can be predicted with reasonable accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of pumps and fittings can be predicted with reasonable accuracy by applying the viscosity model of Hansen.

the ice slurry system is reliable in the investigated concentration range and the flow behaviour is not very different from that of water, which makes ice slurry an attractive alternative to conventional chilled water systems.
the ice slurry system components can be selected in a way that they are able to handle the ice slurry without any problems.
